input: Strings contain only ASCII characters U+0000 through U+007F, so Python code-point and JavaScript UTF-16 code-unit indexing agree. Arbitrary Unicode and boxed strings are outside the paired domain. haystack and needle are strings of lengths n and m in [0, 4294967295]; empty strings are accepted. String inputs, when present, are ordinary str values, not subclasses. Integer values are plain int, excluding bool; lists are ordinary lists, not subclasses. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Allocation and runtime resource limits still require qualification; this declared domain is not a capacity or completion guarantee.
return: The smallest zero-based index where needle occurs contiguously in haystack, or -1 when no match exists. An empty needle returns 0, including when haystack is empty. The result is a scalar integer, not a match object or substring.
mutation_aliasing: All inputs, their ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. Only a private prefix-length array is allocated; neither string can be mutated.
numeric: Indices, prefix lengths and the result are exact integers. The largest index arithmetic is at most 4294967295; no input-number arithmetic, bitwise coercion or sentinel collision is used.
complexity: O(n + m + 1) worst-case time and O(m + 1) auxiliary space. The two KMP passes advance indices monotonically; each fallback strictly lowers matched using an already-built prefix entry, so total fallbacks are linear. An empty needle returns in O(1). No slices, repeated substring searches or recursion are used.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 807 UTF-8 bytes, including the Solution class, method signature, every loop, condition, allocation, standard built-in call, annotation/comment where present, whitespace and terminal newline. There are no custom helper definitions, imports, generated implementations or hidden source expansion. Built-in operations are not free: their allocations and work are included in the stated runtime/storage costs. TreeNode, where used, is an explicit caller-owned input shape and no node is constructed. Any eventual judge-interface adapter is additional charged source; method-style interface parity with frozen sources remains unqualified.
